logic: One Scene-owned focus domain coordinates both source canonical control focus and source popup entry. Its native client elements are the canvas, that surface controls root and native popup receiver; download/product tools, annotations, composer and other HTML surfaces are external.

Focusin, trusted pointerdown and trusted keydown change this ordinary local ownership. Pointermove and paired frame presentation do not create ownership or React state updates. Explicit external pointer interaction retires ownership even while the previous native input remains active.

Canonical control values, selection bookkeeping, geometry and Canvas publication continue according to F3 input-sequence confirmation. DOM focus follows the source only while this HTML domain remains active and the current active element belongs to it or is its temporary document-body state. External active elements preserve focus.

Source blur and popup receiver removal preserve the existing HTML domain. With no source-focused control, its client canvas receives keys; a later source-script focus change can follow inside that active domain. Actual focus calls occur only when the receiver differs.

An active source popup keeps its client keyboard receiver. A popup arriving after the user moved to an external editor does not call focus. No synthetic source-native focus/blur action is sent on client domain departure.
